Matchups, Cooldowns & Lane Priority

Win lane before it starts: learn matchups efficiently, track enemy Flash and key abilities, punish cooldown windows, and use lane priority to win 2v2s with your jungler.

Learn matchups the smart way

There are more than 170 champions. You can't memorize every matchup, so focus on the questions that matter in each one:

  1. Who is stronger at levels 1-3? That decides whether you fight for the first wave or play safe.
  2. Who is stronger at 6? Some champions win lane the moment they get their ultimate.
  3. What is their one ability that matters most? Usually it's their crowd control or their escape. When it's down, you can fight.
  4. Who scales better? If they win late, you need to get ahead early; if you win late, just survive.

Our champion guides list the hardest and easiest matchups for each champion, with a tip for each. After a game you lost in lane, read about that one matchup. That's how you learn the ones you actually face.

Pro tipKeep a small champion pool (2-3 champions per role). You'll learn each matchup from your champion's point of view much faster than if you play 15 different champions.

Tracking Flash and summoner spells

Flash has a 300-second (5-minute) cooldown. When an enemy uses it, they're much easier to kill until it comes back. Pros track this all game, and you can too:

  • When an enemy Flashes, write the time in chat for your team. Press Enter, then type something like "mid flash 12:40" (that's when it's back: the current time + 5 minutes).
  • Also note Teleport, Ignite (180 seconds), Heal and Exhaust (240 seconds), and Barrier (180 seconds).
  • In the scoreboard (Tab), you can click on enemy summoner spells to ping their cooldowns to your team automatically.

Remember that the rune Cosmic Insight gives summoner spell haste, so Flash can come back a little sooner on enemies who take it.

A laner without Flash is your jungler's favorite target. Ping it and ask for a gank.

Common mistakeForgetting that YOU used Flash. If your Flash is down and the enemy jungler goes missing, play much safer. You have no escape.

Fight in the cooldown windows

Most trades in lane happen because one player used an important ability and the other punishes it before it comes back. This is a cooldown window.

Examples:

  • Ahri throws Charm (12-second cooldown) and misses: walk up and trade for the next few seconds.
  • Caitlyn uses her net to jump back: she can't escape again for a while, so your support can engage.
  • Lux misses her Light Binding: she has no crowd control and is very weak until it returns.
  • An enemy uses their dash to farm a minion: now they can't dodge your skill shot.

You can see cooldowns by clicking an enemy champion: their abilities appear at the top of your screen. Hover over the ability to see its exact cooldown at its current rank. Our champion pages also list each ability's cooldown.

Lane priority and why it matters

Lane priority means your wave is pushing toward the enemy, so you can leave lane first and they can't follow without losing minions. Priority is what lets you help your jungler at Scuttle, roam, or arrive first at Dragon.

To get priority:

  • Push the wave faster than your opponent, using abilities on minions when it's safe.
  • Win trades so they have to back off and lose minions.
  • Recall after crashing a wave into their turret, not while your wave is pushing toward yours. See Recall Timing and Tempo.

Mid lane priority is especially valuable, because the mid laner is closest to both sides of the river and can help at every objective.

Playing for 2v2s with your jungler

The early game is often decided by 2v2 fights: your laner and jungler against theirs. Whoever has priority wins these, because they get to the fight first.

Use jungle tracking (see Tracking the Enemy Jungler) to guess where both junglers are:

  • If your jungler is coming to your side of the map and you have priority, push your wave and walk toward the river with them.
  • If the enemy jungler is on your side and your jungler is far away, push the wave carefully or stay near your turret.
  • Around the first Scuttle (2:55) and Void Grubs (8:00), the laners nearby with priority decide who gets them.

Communicate simply: ping your jungler's portrait or use "On my way" pings to show you're ready to help.

Pro tipWhen your jungler is fighting the enemy jungler near your lane, getting there first is everything. Push your wave a little before your jungler arrives so you can move instantly.

Key takeaways

  • For each matchup, know: who wins levels 1-3, who wins at 6, their key ability, and who scales better.
  • Flash has a 5-minute cooldown. Write enemy Flash timers in chat.
  • Trade when the enemy just used an important ability.
  • Lane priority (your wave pushing) lets you move first to fights and objectives.
  • Early 2v2s are won by the side whose laner gets there first.
